title: Bjarne Stroustrup and the Making of C++ (1979-1985)
explainer: In 1979 Bjarne Stroustrup began extending C with Simula-style classes at Bell Labs, aiming for a language 'as elegant as Simula, yet as efficient as C'; he called the result 'C with Classes,' renamed it C++ in 1983, and released it publicly in 1985. Templates were added afterward specifically so that language could express compile-time generic code without giving up C's low-level control. That origin explains why advanced C++ still reads as a fusion of two eras: a C-compatible core with a much later, much richer type and template system layered on top.

title: Move Semantics' Decade-Long Road to C++11
explainer: Rvalue references and move semantics were not an overnight addition: Howard Hinnant, Dave Abrahams, and Peter Dimov first proposed the '&&' reference type to the C++ standards committee in 2002 (paper N1377), motivated by how utilities like auto_ptr silently transferred ownership when they claimed to copy. The proposal went through several more revisions before rvalue references and move semantics were finally standardized in C++11, nearly a decade later. That history is why move semantics can feel layered on top of a language that already had working copy constructors and destructors - it was.
